title: AgentSociety: Large-Scale Simulation of LLM-Driven Generative Agents Advances Understanding of Human Behaviors and Society
notes: Local PDF is available and initial review confirms strong multi-agent social simulation. Binary-level PDF checks also expose mobility- and map-related traces such as mobility_behavior, OpenStreetMap, CityFlow, hurricanes, and urban sustainability, which support an explicit environment-side spatial structure. The remaining uncertainty is representational granularity for later coding, not whether the paper belongs in Core screening.

title: When LLMs Recognize Your Space: Research on Experiences with Spatially Aware LLM Agents
notes: Local reading note plus public abstract are already sufficient. This is a human-agent interaction study about spatial awareness improving counselling-style conversations, not a multi-agent social simulation. It remains valuable as Adjacent evidence that spatial context matters for interaction quality.

title: A Context-Aware Onboarding Agent for Metaverse Powered by Large Language Models
notes: Primary-source abstract shows an LLM-based onboarding pipeline for first-time metaverse users that answers questions using short-term spatiotemporal context and long-term exploration history. The metaverse setting is explicit, but the system is still a single-agent onboarding assistant rather than a multi-agent social simulation.

title: A Voice-Controlled Dialogue System for NPC Interaction using Large Language Models
notes: ACL source and downloaded PDF confirm a Unity-based voice interface that maps a player's spoken paraphrases onto predefined dialogue options for NPC interaction. This is situated and game-world based, but it is a single user-to-NPC interface study rather than a multi-agent social system.

title: Mixed-Initiative Dialogue Management for Human-Virtual Agents Interaction in Forum Theatre Inspired Training
notes: ACL source and downloaded PDF confirm a VR training tool with autonomous virtual agents and one conversational agent guiding reflection and replay. The environment and social scene are explicit, but the paper is best treated as a human-agent training interaction case, not Core social simulation evidence.

title: TongSIM: A General Platform for Simulating Intelligent Machines
notes: ArXiv source and downloaded PDF confirm a high-fidelity embodied platform with 100 plus indoor scenes, an open-ended outdoor town, and support for composite activities including multi-agent social simulation and human-AI collaboration. However, at the paper level it still reads primarily as a general simulator platform and benchmark resource, so Adjacent is the safer current placement unless later method reading reveals concrete social-system evidence central enough to justify Core.

title: S^3: Social-network Simulation System with Large Language Model-Empowered Agents
notes: Primary-source review confirms this is the 2023 arXiv paper at 2307.14984, and the local arXiv PDF is now archived. The paper clearly supports LLM multi-agent collective behavior in a structured social-network environment. Under the accepted conservative boundary, however, structured digital social platforms are treated as relevant but not Core-defining environments, so this paper should stabilize in Adjacent.

title: Unveiling the collective behaviors of large language model-based autonomous agents in an online community: A social network analysis perspective
notes: Primary-source review confirms an open-access study of LLM-based autonomous agents in Chirper, a structured online community with profiles, posts, follows, replies, and interaction histories. Multi-agent interaction and collective behavior are explicit, but the operative environment is still a digital social platform rather than a physical or navigable virtual space. Official PDF endpoint attempts returned anti-bot HTML, and under the accepted conservative boundary this paper belongs in Adjacent, so more Core-oriented download effort is unnecessary.
